knowledge-base.overview: Spring Boot 3.x / Java 17+ guardrails, patterns, and best practices for enterprise REST APIs and microservices. Covers layered architecture (Controller/Service/Repository), constructor injection, DTO records with Bean Validation, JPA entities, Flyway migrations, Spring Security (stateless JWT), GlobalExceptionHandler with ProblemDetail (RFC 7807), Testcontainers integration tests, and OpenAPI documentation. Loaded automatically when agents work on Spring Boot Java projects.

core-principles.principle: Leverage Spring Boot auto-configuration. Override only when necessary.
Controller -> Service -> Repository with clear separation. Controllers handle HTTP only; Services contain all business logic and transactions; Repositories handle data access.
Never expose JPA entities in API responses. Use Java records as DTOs.
Use @RequiredArgsConstructor or explicit constructors. Never @Autowired on fields.
All configuration via application.yml with profile-specific overrides. Secrets via environment variables.
Schema changes through Flyway or Liquibase only. Never ddl-auto=update in production.

guardrail.rule: Never use @Autowired on fields. Use constructor injection with @RequiredArgsConstructor or explicit constructors.
guardrail.bad: @Autowired private UserRepository userRepository; // field injection — BLOCKER

guardrail.rule: Never expose JPA entities in API responses. Always map to DTO records before returning from service layer.
Never use ddl-auto=update in production. Use Flyway or Liquibase migrations.
Always annotate request body parameters with @Valid on controllers.
Keep spring.jpa.open-in-view=false. Lazy loading must occur within a transaction.
Use @Transactional(readOnly = true) at the service class level and @Transactional on write methods individually.
Return ProblemDetail (RFC 7807) from all exception handlers. Never return custom error formats.
Use @PageableDefault for list endpoints. Never return unbounded collections.
Use @OneConfiguration class per concern (SecurityConfig, WebConfig, CacheConfig). Never put multiple concerns in one @Configuration class.
Use MapStruct for entity-DTO mapping. Never write manual mapping boilerplate.
Use Testcontainers for integration tests. Never use H2 as a production substitute for a real database.
